issue_context.title: Provide opt-in for custom converters to handle null
comments: In case anyone needs a solution to this problem specifically to be able to serialize an empty `IList<T>` as `null` instead of `[]`, I created a wrapper class. See [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/37599).

review_comments: Isn't `IgnoreNullValues` going to be obsoleted at some point?
We have to support the current semantics for as long as it's in the public API.

"https://default" instead?

Or are you checking to see if we call the correct converter? Is so, please comment.

Here, the reference type converter doesn't override `HandleNull`, so the property is false. The serializer will set the default value when deserializing and write `null` when serializing. I've added a comment.
@steveharter What was the reason why we were caching `ShouldHandleNullValue` in `HandleNullValue`? Is it ok to get rid of that?
I wondered the same thing. I couldn't tell why we needed `ShouldHandleNullValue`.
Doesn't the same feedback from https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/35826#discussion_r421023122 appies to this  and to all other generic types annotated?
These annotate the return values, not input parameters. These annotations correctly note that `null` may be returned even though the type may be non-nullable (depending on the JSON payload).
Ah I see what you mean. Even though `T` was a non-nullable reference type, we may return `T?`.

> Even though T was a non-nullable reference type, we may return T?.

Even if T is a non-nullable reference type, we may return `null`.
Doesn't the converter return `Point_2D(-1, -1)` (not null) for TokenType.Null?
By default, reference types don't handle `null` tokens, so the serializer handles `null` (sets the default value). The comment a couple lines above mentions this.
So the original code here was not called for ClassType==Value? Or was this optimization not necessary?

This branch was unreachable, as the converter is of type `JsonDictionaryConverter<T> ` which cannot be `ClassType.Value`. We branched into a separate path for custom (`ClassType.Value`) converters. This change should have been made in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/34569.
If you remove `[return: MaybeNull]` from https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/35826/files#diff-56b52018b267905bd21daf4c7615b6c7R108 you can then remove this `!`.

Annotating the converter's `Read` method was part of the feedback from API review - https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/34439#issuecomment-622040198, since now it could return `null` (since we can now pass `JsonTokenType.Null` to it).
Not used. Also suggest to have "Uri" in the name.
This is a test method, so there no references to this. I wanted to have the generic because the behavior is them same for all reference types, not just Uri.
